cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Be Right in Retrospect
cards.instruction: Perform certainty by reinterpreting every surprise as something your earlier words were obviously predicting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I turned our tap the way the plumber turned his. I said this evening would flow, and look at the kitchen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He was shutting a valve. You opened the tap over a blocked sink.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, demonstrating flow. Water has become the whole evening's conversation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've shut the main valve. We can mop up, but no taps will run tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the conversation will keep flowing while we mop. You heard me promise an evening of it.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copied valve motion creates a flood claimed as a flow forecast; A3 reinterprets the promise as water conversation; A5 turns B4 no-running-water surprise into continuing conversation during cleanup.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 blocked-sink correction supports A3 water-topic cover; B4 shutoff/mopping supports A5 nonliteral flow that survives the supply ending.

relationship.evidence: B4 acts to contain damage and states the remaining work.

heightening.evidence: A5 preserves certainty by switching the meaning of the same early flow word after B4 removes its literal meaning.

specificity.evidence: A1 tap/flood, B2 blocked sink and B4 no taps plus mopping now distinguish supply from standing water.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 makes B hear the old phrase as accurate without inventing new earlier words.
